To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a metric map of a large dynamic space can be maintained online with stereo vision and that a map can be maintained in spite of occlusion and localization failure by using a probabilistic representation of a map.

(1) a metric map of an environment can be built using only visual input from a stereo pair, (2) a visual SLAM system can be robust to occlusions and localization errors, (3) a metric map can be updated in real time to reflect changes to the environment, (4) a metric map that is built in a single run can be used to initialize a new map, and (5) a map can be maintained and updated in an online, continuous fashion, and
we have developed a system for visual map building and localization in dynamic environments.
